_doc: Claim checks of PDF items against OR Ser. I vol. 27. Generated by tools/bt/or27_claims.py. Verdicts are analyst readings of located passages; they are NOT owner decisions and pick no default. Quotes are < 15 words, located and re-verified by code. Page numbers are recovered from OCR running heads (see or27_index.json page_recovery_checks).

items.pdf_note: PDF p.3 research note says Reynolds's death time, Hancock's arrival time and Ewell's decision time were 'not found' in its source set.

subclaims.claim: Reynolds' death time
subclaims.finding: The OR gives two different times: about 10.15 a.m. for the shot (Doubleday) and 11.15 a.m. for 'killed' (Howard's 5 p.m. dispatch); Howard's later report dates the news of the death 'about 11.30'. 10.15 is among the PDF's values; 11:15 and 11:30 are NOT in the PDF's value list; 10:30 and 10:40-10:50 are not found in the OR. Hunt shows Reynolds still giving an order about 10.15.

evidence.note: Doubleday: Reynolds 'had just been shot, and was no more'; this occurred 'in the beginning of the attack referred to', about 10.15 a.m.
evidence.quote: about 10.15 a. m.

items.topic: Hancock's arrival at Gettysburg / Cemetery Hill (Jul 1)
items.pdf_note: PDF p.3 research note says Hancock's arrival time was 'not found' in its source set.

subclaims.claim: Hancock arrives Jul 1: about 15:00 / before 16:00 / 16:00 / 16:30
subclaims.finding: Hancock's own report: left Taneytown 1.10 p.m., 'At 3 p.m. I arrived at Gettysburg and assumed the command'. His 5.25 p.m. note says he arrived 'an hour since' (about 16:25). Howard's 5 p.m. dispatch and Slocum both say 4 p.m. So 15:00, 16:00 and about 16:25-16:30 all occur; the PDF band 15:00-16:00 spans Hancock's own time and Howard/Slocum. Hancock's note says the troops 'have now taken up a position in the cemetery'; 'Cemetery Hill' is not named as the arrival point.

subclaims.claim: Meade reaches the field after midnight (PDF default about 01:00; alternative about 04:00)
subclaims.finding: Meade's own report: left Taneytown at 10 p.m. on the 1st and arrived at 1 a.m. of the 2d. Hunt says Meade 'reached Gettysburg about 2 a.m.' (a value not in the PDF list). subclaims.claim: Union council of war, Jul 2 (PDF: 21:00 / midnight / late; window 21:00-24:00)
subclaims.supports_pdf_default: partly (no OR start time; one witness has it running to nearly 12)
subclaims.finding: The OR places the council on the 'evening'/'night' of July 2 (Butterfield's minutes are headed 'Thursday p. m., July 2'). The only clock time found is Gibbon's (letter of March 1864): the sitting 'continued up to nearly 12 o'clock'; Newton's letter says 'the night of the 2d' and Sedgwick's 'the evening'; Gibbon places it after the Third Corps' defeat that afternoon. No OR passage found gives a start hour. A separate passage in a pro-Sickles extract (printed in Meade's volume) speaks of Sickles being summoned to a council of corps commanders before the attack opened that afternoon ('the council is over'), which suggests a second, earlier meeting; no clock time.

items.topic: Hunt, Jul 3: batteries 04:30/05:30, 10:00 orders, cannonade, ceasefire

subclaims.claim: Jul 3 morning guns open: 04:30 vs 05:30
subclaims.supports_pdf_default: yes (default 05:30), and the OR shows both values are true events
subclaims.finding: Hunt: at 1 a.m. Muhlenberg's and Kinzie's batteries were posted opposite the Twelfth Corps line; 'At 4.30 a.m. these batteries opened' and fired fifteen minutes into the wood; Rigby's battery was added soon after daylight and at 5.30 a.m. all the batteries opened, firing at intervals until 10 a.m., when the infantry drove the enemy out. So 04:30 is the first two batteries (15 min), 05:30 is the full battery line.

subclaims.claim: E. P. Alexander's own account of the Jul 3 cannonade
subclaims.finding: Alexander's Report No. 464 (pp.429-431) covers July 2 only; for July 3 it says the battalion 'remained near and in rear of its original position on the 2d until 4 p. m.' and then marched to Black Horse Tavern. It gives no cannonade start/end and no signal-gun account. Alexander's role on July 3 appears only in Longstreet's report (posted batteries and agreed the signal; was sent to a point to watch the effect and told Pickett the time had come).

items.topic: Stuart / Hampton / Jenkins: arrival (Jul 2) and where Jenkins was wounded

pdf.pdf_printed_default: Stuart himself early afternoon, brigades in the evening

subclaims.claim: Stuart's arrival time (PDF: noon-13:00 / mid-afternoon / afternoon / evening; default Stuart early afternoon, brigades evening)
subclaims.supports_pdf_default: no support either way (date confirmed, clock time absent)
subclaims.finding: Stuart's report: dispatch from Lee reached him during the night of July 1 at Carlisle; 'My advance reached Gettysburg July 2, just in time to thwart a move of the enemy's cavalry upon our rear by way of Hunterstown'; he took position that day on the York and Heidlersburg roads. No hour is given. Hampton: his brigade 'was stationed on July 2, at Hunterstown, 5 miles to the east of Gettysburg' when ordered up, fought Union cavalry between Hunterstown and Gettysburg, held the ground through the night. Lee (July 1863 report) records only the afternoon-of-July-1 news that Stuart had reached Carlisle.
